parts.transcript: Part 2: a radio presenter describes the Elmsden Way cycle route (Elmsden Station to Langton). Map: from the station the path runs east, north around the lake; Rocks east of the road just before it goes under the railway (11=B); at the fork the road continues straight to Colleen Nature Reserve (12=E); the path follows River Cleve south to the Ashington China Factory (13=F); after the bridge, Langton Forest is to the south (14=I). Warnings/info: watch for sheep/animals (15=C); Elmsden Station re-opened recently (16=C); the visitor's centre hires bikes (17=A); trains between the two stations run only at weekends, no booking/charge (18=B); River Elm walk takes a long time, steep climb back (19=A); full details of local routes in the Saturday local paper (20=A).

parts.title: Photic sneezing
parts.transcript: Part 4: a Health Sciences lecture on photic (light) sneezing. Background: some react to sunlight with a prickle in the nose, faster breathing (31) and watery eyes, relieved by a sneeze; this photic sneeze can't be controlled and is a common reflex (32). Sneezing: caused by irritation in the nose; nerve endings in the face are stimulated (33); coordinated by the same mechanism that controls tears (34). Research: Aristotle asked why the sun, but not the heat of a fire (35), causes sneezing; Bacon showed it was due to light; Everett found 80% of sneezers had relatives (36) who sneeze. Indicators: sneezers produce the same number of sneezes (37); caused by a contrast (38) in brightness; the sneeze needs time (39) to recharge. Application: largely ignored except research on photic sneezing among pilots (40); may lead to breakthroughs for migraine/epilepsy.

Photic sneezing

Background

Some people react to sunlight by:

This ‘photic’ sneeze cannot be controlled and is a reflex.

Sneezing in general
